subject: Time-boxed residency carveout + escrowed audit creds for pilot - exec clearance needed
messages:
From: Samuel Price <samuel.price@veridianhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot request — residency and audit scope questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Veridian's technical team is keen to move forward with a 6-week pilot, but we have two gating items before procurement can issue an SOW:

1) Data residency: we need a guarantee that all customer data for the pilot will reside in a US-only region and not be replicated outside the continental US.
2) Audit / forensic access: for this pilot, our security team requests the ability to run a time-boxed forensic review if we suspect a data event — limited to a single 30-day window during and immediately after the pilot. They indicated that we could work with a third-party auditor and would require an agreed evidence package (logs, access records, host inventory).

Can Redwood accommodate a US-only residency for the pilot and agree to a tightly-scoped, time-limited audit right (with oversight and redaction for shared infra)? Also, procurement asked whether a pilot discount is possible given this non-standard ask.

Attaching our security questionnaire and a short SOW template.

Thanks,
Samuel Price
Sr. Cloud Security Manager
Veridian Health
Attachments: veridian_security_questionnaire.xlsx, SOW_template.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samuel Price <samuel.price@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-09T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — residency and audit scope questions

Samuel — appreciate the clear ask and the questionnaire.

Short answer: we can support a US-only residency for a time-boxed pilot and we are open to a scoped forensic review under strict controls, but this is a nonstandard term that requires legal + deal desk signoff.

Proposal from my side to keep the pilot moving:
- Residency: provision a dedicated VPC in our us-west-2 region and restrict backups/replication to that region for the pilot duration.
- Audit: agree to a single, documented 30-day forensic window performed by an agreed third-party auditor. Redwood would provide a predefined evidence package (access logs, KV cache traces, config snapshots) and would redact any PII unrelated to the incident.
- Controls: auditor access must be via a read-only, time-limited mechanism; we will require an NDA with the auditor and an explicit statement of scope.
- Commercial: we can offer a 10% pilot credit on hosted usage and waive onboarding fees, subject to exec approval for the non-standard audit term and residency commitment.

Lauren & Ben — can you weigh in on legal guardrails and whether the 10%/waived-fees ask is approvable at deal desk level or needs VP signoff? If you agree, I will send a short amendment and a DocuSign link.

Samuel — copying procurement and security on the next iteration. Thanks for the patience.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-12T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — residency and audit scope questions

Marissa / Ben — reviewed Samuel's asks and Marissa's proposed guardrails. Legal recommendations and constraints below: 

1) Residency carveout: acceptable as a pilot-only contractual appendix. Language should state explicitly: "Data processed for the Pilot will be provisioned and stored in the us-west-2 region and will not be replicated outside the continental United States for the duration of the Pilot (Pilot Period)." Include an explicit end date / auto-revert clause.

2) Forensic review: approve a time-boxed forensic window limited to one occurrence during the Pilot Period + a 30-day evidence-retention window. We must:
- Require a written incident trigger (reasonable suspicion threshold),
- Approve the identity and scope for the third-party auditor in advance,
- Require auditor to execute Redwood's standard auditor NDA and a narrow statement-of-work, and
- Limit the evidence package to logs and metadata (no full disk images or arbitrary host access).

3) Escrowed credentials / redaction: recommend using an escrow process where proof artifacts are transmitted via an encrypted, auditable transfer; Redwood will perform redaction of unrelated tenant data prior to delivery where feasible. If redaction risk is high, require a scoped on-site observation (or remote screen-sharing) rather than broad credential escrow.

4) Commercial concession: legal can support a pilot credit up to 12% total (credits + waived onboarding) but any discount >12% or permanent SLA modifications require VP Revenue signoff. We should also cap the engineering effort: include an acceptance criterion that any custom infra changes for the pilot are limited to an agreed list and that Redwood reserves the right to bill for out-of-scope engineering at standard T&M rates if requested.

Attachments: proposed_mop.pdf (short MOP for pilot), redwood_auditor_ndas.txt

If we proceed, I'll draft the Pilot Appendix and a slim amendment for signature. Marissa — do you want Legal to draft the DocuSign envelope or should Sales prepare the deal record first?

—Lauren Bishop
Principal Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, Samuel Price <samuel.price@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-14T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — residency and audit scope questions

All — technical confirmation and runway / pricing notes.

We can stand up a dedicated VPC in us-west-2 and flip replication off for the pilot. Engineering will tag pilot data and enable verbose logging (retained for 90 days internally) to support the evidence package. A few important operational notes:
- If Veridian requests host-level artifacts beyond logs (e.g., core dumps), that will require elevated access discussions and likely not feasible for a hosted multi-tenant control plane.
- We can provide an export of access logs, API call traces, and deployment manifests for the agreed 30-day window.
- Any on-demand, out-of-scope troubleshooting (work that requires core infra changes or blue/green swaps) will be billed at our established T&M rates — include a provision in the MOP.

Commercially: sales ops — please confirm whether the 12% combined credit cap is acceptable. If Sales wants a deeper concession, we need revenue VP signoff (per Legal).

Samuel — if the above matches Veridian's needs, I'll ask Sales to post the Pilot Appendix to HubSpot and generate a DocuSign for signature (link attached). Otherwise, flag items that must change.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Customer Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_mop.pdf
